760	Competitor example: `MB_E_CLASS` with `is_bmw_group:0`, `profile_json:{competes_with:["G60","G68"], markets:[…], strengths:"Comfort and ride, luxury image, MBUX Superscreen", global_2025:461201, …}`. No page shows the competitor models today.
761	
762	**market** (US): `{code:"US", name:"United States", countries_json:["US"], climate:"Wide range: …", usage_patterns:"High annual mileage (~13,500 miles…)", cultural_expectations:"Affordability pressure…; tech must work…", infrastructure:"Jan 2025: 207,227 public charging ports…", powertrain_mix:"EV share peaked at ~12%…", profile_source_ids_json:[…], profile_valid_from:"2026-10-10"}`
763	RoW has `countries_json:["*"]`. **No page shows the market profiles today**, even though D-011 says "markets are different customers". A market endpoint and card would support that story.
764	
765	**llm_usage**: `{id, created_at, settled_at, job:"fit:sol", demo:0, kind:"responses"|"embeddings", model:"gpt-6.1-sol", service_tier:"flex", status:"completed"|"reserved"|"failed", reserved_usd, cost_usd:0.00647, input_tokens:3499, cached_tokens:0, cache_write_tokens:3496, output_tokens:420, reasoning_tokens:39, search_calls:0, response_id, error}`
766	Spend by prefix (USD): derive 2.67, research 1.69, reconciliation 1.00, fit 0.61, extract 0.52, link 0.28, challenge 0.17, recheck 0.13, bench 0.09, consolidate 0.09, …
767	
768	### Confidentiality map
769	| Data | Class | Notes |
770	|---|---|---|
771	| `source_item.text`/`quote` (feedback), `signal.quote`/`need_statement`, `finding_source.quote`, `meta_json.bmw_labels`/`excel_rows` | **BMW confidential** | Serve on localhost only |
772	| `kind=study` items, `study_metric`, finding summaries quoting means/z | **BMW confidential** | |
773	| `sales` (stylized BMW-internal, Q-015) | **BMW confidential** | Relative use only; never blend with public data |
774	| `option_list` incl. `price_eur` | **BMW confidential** (from the PDF) | Prices are out of scope; don't display them |
775	| Requirements, findings, breakdowns, audit | **Derived from confidential data** | Same handling |
776	| web / reference items | Public, cited | |
777	| Sketchfab 3D models | Third-party CC BY | Only camera moves go out |
778	
779	---
780	
781	## 5. Domain vocabulary (UI labels) and PM workflow
782	
783	**Plain labels** (`ui/common.py`):
784	- `VEHICLE_NAMES` = F70 "1 Series", G60 "5 Series", G68 "5 Series LWB", G70 "7 Series"
785	- `MARKET_SHORT` = US "USA", EU "Europe", CN "China", RoW "Rest of world". `MARKET_NAMES` has full names ("United States").
786	- `plain_target("G60","US")` → "5 Series · USA". Internal label: `tlabel` → "G60 × US".
787	- `EVIDENCE_LABELS` = E1 "Strong evidence", E2 "Good evidence", E3 "Limited evidence", E4 "Assumption only". `EVIDENCE_HELP`:
788	  - E1: 20+ comments from 2+ channels, plus study or cited web
789	  - E2: 15+ comments, or comments plus study/web
790	  - E3: a few comments, or study/web only
791	  - E4: no direct evidence, forward-looking assumption
792	- `KANO_LABELS` = basic "Expected", performance "Differentiator", delighter "Delighter"
793	- `HORIZON_LABELS` = today "Needed today", at_successor_launch "Needed by successor launch"
794	- `STATUS_LABELS` = proposed "To review", challenged "Challenged", approved "Approved", deferred "Deferred", rejected "Rejected"
795	- `PRIORITIES` = Must, Should, Could. Bands: Must ≥ 60, Should ≥ 45. The chip for AI priorities reads "{p} · AI suggests".
796	- Proposal kinds (inbox): priority "Priority changes", content "Content edits", link_finding "Evidence links", new_requirement "New requirements", extend "Merge into existing", status "Status". Proposal states: open, accepted, rejected, superseded.
797	- Challenge verdicts: upheld "You're right", partially_upheld "Partly right", not_upheld "The evidence holds".
798	- Fit check types: brand = "gate", market = "score modifier" (pass +2, warn −5, fail −10), segment = "shown", feasibility = "context" (non-blocking, D-030). Results: pass, warn, fail, plus a derived "overridden".
799	- Realization: carry_over, platform_wide, derivative_specific, market_variant, package. Effort S/M/L (modifiers 0/−3/−6).
800	- Who chips (journey): ai "AI", system "System · no AI", human "Product manager".
801	- Factor labels: Customer voice, Satisfaction gap, Market volume, Competitive pressure, Future relevance, Portfolio leverage.
802	- Trust tiers: T1 official/primary, T2 established press/analysts, T3 forums/blogs.
803	- Waves:
804	  - Wave 1 "Concept kick-off", simulated 2026-11: half the verbatims, 2024 sales, options, reference data, baseline web research
805	  - Wave 2 "+6 months", 2027-05: the other half of the verbatims, study 2025, sales 2025 and 2030
806	  - Wave 3 "+12 months, market event", 2027-11: new web research
807	- Always labelled with the **SIMULATION** badge.
808	
809	**Colors** (`COLORS[key] = (fg, bg)`):
810	
811	| Key | fg | bg |
812	|---|---|---|
813	| Must | #ffffff | #1c69d4 (BMW blue) |
814	| Should | #0b3d7a | #d6e6fb |
815	| Could | #4a5563 | #eceff3 |
816	| proposed | #0b3d7a | #e3edfb |
817	| challenged | #5b2a86 | #efe5f8 |
818	| approved | #0f5132 | #d8f0e2 |
819	| deferred | #7a4b00 | #fff1d0 |
820	| rejected | #842029 | #f8dcdf |
821	| E1 | #0f5132 | #cfeedd |
822	| E2 | #1d5a3a | #e3f4ea |
823	| E3 | #7a4b00 | #fff1d0 |
824	| E4 | #842029 | #f8dcdf |
825	
826	- pass, warn, fail and overridden reuse the green, amber, red and purple pairs. human, ai and system reuse green, blue and grey.
827	- EVIDENCE, ASSUMPTION, UNCERTAINTY and CONFLICT are green, amber, red and red.
828	- T1, T2 and T3 are green, amber and red.
829	- open, accepted and superseded are blue, green and grey.
830	- `FACTOR_COLOR` #1c69d4; `NO_DATA_COLOR` #c9d0d8.
831	- Cards have left borders: evidence #2e8b57, assumption #d99a00, uncertainty and conflict #c0392b.
832	
833	**Demo tour (`TOUR` in `app.py`), the PM story as told today:**
834	1. **Home**, "The question and where we are": BMW asks what the next 5, 1 and 7 Series should offer. The AI turned 10k comments, a study, sales and web research into ranked requirements. Three simulated waves stand for ~2 years.
835	2. **How it works**, "Follow one requirement, step by step": comment → signal → theme → requirement → brand/market fit → score arithmetic → PM decision → re-scoring. Left is the rule, right is the effect.
836	3. **Review**, "Review one requirement": the need, the evidence (comments, study, competitors), the AI's priority per car × market. The PM approves, rejects or defers, always with a reason.
837	4. **Priorities by market**, "Markets are different customers": 5 Series · USA vs 5 Series LWB · China. China has no comments, so it rests on study and web evidence, which is shown, not hidden.
838	5. **AI suggestions**, "The AI suggests, the PM decides": after new evidence, priority changes with their cause, new requirements, and merges instead of duplicates.
839	6. **Requirement details**, "Full traceability": score breakdown, evidence chain to the comment, brand/market fit, and "brand-fit FAIL blocks approval".
840	7. **Audit trail**, "Complete audit trail": who, when, why, model. Append-only (DB triggers reject UPDATE and DELETE).
841	8. **Export**, "The deliverable": ID, description, findings and sources, score and rationale, evidence level, assumptions and uncertainties, status.
842	
843	The tour skips the 3D car view, Market conflicts, Findings, Quality hand-over, Portfolio, Weights and Budget.
844	
845	---
846	
847	## 6. Honest assessment: confusing, redundant, out of workflow
848	
849	**A. Too many overlapping views of the same thing: requirements ranked per car × market (six of them).** Home "Top priorities", Priorities by market (board plus compare), All requirements (table, also with a compare mode), Market conflicts, Portfolio coverage (priority counts) and the 3D car view all render `targets_df()` sliced by target. Board-compare and Backlog-compare are near-duplicates, and Conflicts is a third "compare markets" view. Suggestion: one **Priorities** workspace with view modes (board, table, compare, 3D) and a "show conflicts only" filter.
850	
851	**B. Two places to decide, with diverging forms.** Review has approve, defer and reject plus "also accept AI priorities", plus Ask-AI. Details › PM decision has approve, reject, defer and **back to proposed**, plus per-target priorities, gate override, edit content, evidence links and challenge. The challenge UI exists twice with different labels and colors. The gate override exists **only** on Details, so if Review blocks approval the PM must leave the flow. Suggestion: one requirement workspace (the Review layout) with the decision panel always docked and the deep tabs (Score, Evidence, Fit, Audit) beneath. The queue becomes a sidebar list.
852	
853	**C. Three "how it works" explanations.** The Home step cards, How it works (8 steps) and Pipeline & data (workflow graph plus the "Who does what" table) all explain the pipeline. How it works is the good one. The overview graph and funnel could be one section of it, and the Home cards could be a single link.
854	
855	**D. Requirement selection is inconsistent.** Review uses a queue with Prev/Next. Details and How it works use a giant selectbox of "REQ-xxxx · title" and share `session_state.req_id`, so opening one silently changes the other. Board, Home and 3D all jump to Review. The Inbox and Findings jump to Details. A URL-routed `/requirements/:id` fixes this.
856	
857	**E. The wave control is buried and the state is confusing.** "Open next wave" sits only on Home, behind the dialog. Pipeline & data says "the wave timeline is on Home". The current DB is at wave 3, so the button never appears and there is no reset in the UI (it needs the CLI `demo_state.py`, with the app stopped). The wave is the spine of the ~2-year story, so it belongs in a persistent header or timeline, with progress streaming and a job status. It currently blocks the page for minutes.
858	
859	**F. Labels and terms drift.**
860	- Nav says "All requirements (table)", but the page header says "Backlog".
861	- Nav says "Portfolio coverage", but the header says "Portfolio".
862	- Details shows raw codes (`E1`, `basic`, `at_successor_launch`, `approved` chips, "Kano: basic"), while Review, Board and Home use plain labels ("Strong evidence", "Expected", "To review").
863	- Backlog and Conflicts show raw "G60 × US", while other pages say "5 Series · USA".
864	- The Details challenge copy says "Change inbox", while the nav says "AI suggestions".
865	- The Weights caption says confidence "E4 ×0.65", but the code has 0.5.
866	- Inbox tabs show "Status" for a kind that, when accepted, does nothing.
867	
868	**G. Data shown is stale relative to the rules.** The DB is score-v2 and derive-v6, so "The decision this asks for", `cap_note` and `priority_note` never render, and Expected needs show mixed priorities across markets, which contradicts the rule printed in How it works step 6 and in the Details caption. A demo viewer could catch this. Re-score (free) before the demo; re-derive for `product_decision`.
869	
870	**H. Evidence-chain gaps.** No page shows the full requirement → finding → **signal** → verbatim chain for a requirement. The Details evidence tab jumps from finding to source quotes; signals appear only for one example in How it works. The Details graph caps at 14 findings. REQ-0001 has 36 links, so most of its evidence is invisible in the graph.
871	
872	**I. Audit and access gaps.**
873	- The Quality hand-over CSV download isn't logged as an export (all other downloads are).
874	- Proposal creation (by runs and challenges) has no audit event of its own; it is visible only in `change_proposal`.
875	- `decide_proposal` isn't atomic.
876	- `challenge()` leaves the status at `challenged` if the LLM fails.
877	- An `override_gate` persists across later fit failures.
878	- "Previous challenges" pairs questions to answers by list order.
879	
880	**J. The PM loses context on actions.** Most writes `st.rerun()` and show a flash at the top of the page. In Review, "Record decision" with "include decided" off removes the item from the queue, so it jumps to the next requirement without a summary of what was recorded. The inbox has no bulk accept ("accept all priority changes with one rationale"), although that is the most common action after a wave.
881	
882	**K. Unused or missing in the UI despite being in the data/story:**
883	- Market profiles (`market` table; this is the D-011 story)
884	- Competitor models (`vehicle_model` with `is_bmw_group=0`)
885	- Brand guardrails (`brand.guardrails_json`, which gates approval, D-031)
886	- The 755 uncovered findings as an actionable "gaps" queue (it's only a filter today)
887	- Kano drift and must-not-lose filters
888	
889	**L. "Under the hood" mixes PM tools with dev diagnostics.** Weights & runs is a real PM lever (D-013, "re-prioritize") and should sit near Priorities. Budget, Pipeline & data and the raw table are diagnostics. Portfolio coverage is a strong PM view (evidence gaps per market) but sits under "Under the hood".
890	
891	**Suggested PM-workflow IA for the rewrite** (for discussion):
892	1. **Overview**: question, wave timeline (open next wave), to-dos.
893	2. **Inbox**: new requirements, merges, priority changes and content edits, with bulk actions.
894	3. **Review**: queue plus a requirement workspace with decision, priorities, override, edit, links and challenge, and deep tabs.
895	4. **Priorities**: board, table, compare, conflicts and 3D as view modes, with portfolio gaps.
896	5. **Evidence**: findings explorer, uncovered findings, quality hand-over.
897	6. **History**: audit, runs diff and weights.
898	7. **Deliver**: export.
899	8. **System**: budget and pipeline stats.
900	
901	The "How it works" walkthrough stays as a guided overlay launched from any requirement.
902

# Successor API — contract v1 (FastAPI, `api/`, 127.0.0.1:8600)

Source of truth for semantics: `scratchpad/inventory.md` (§1–§4). This file fixes the endpoint list and shapes for the NEW
information architecture: Briefing · Decide · Cars · Requirement · Evidence · Process. JSON keys are snake_case.

## Conventions
- Target object: `{vehicle:"G60", market:"US", key:"G60×US", label:"5 Series · USA", car:"5 Series", market_label:"USA"}` (`×` = U+00D7).
- Priorities on a target: `pm_priority` (PM-confirmed or null), `ai_priority` (proposed_priority), `priority` = pm ?? ai, `ai_only` bool.
- Labels come from `/api/meta`; the API returns codes (E1, basic, proposed…) and the frontend maps to labels.
- Writes: JSON body always includes `rationale` (≥5 chars) except where noted; actor comes from header `X-Actor` (default "Atahan (PM)"). `ActionError` → HTTP 409 `{detail: message}`. Validation errors → 422. Missing entity → 404.
- One shared sqlite connection (`bmw_req.db.connect()` once), all access serialized by a process-wide `threading.RLock` (reads too — sqlite connection is not thread-safe). Never wrap service writes in your own transaction.
- Long jobs (wave open, challenge) run in a background thread with their OWN connection (they open their own anyway), registered in an in-memory job table.
- Every GET of a requirement detail does NOT log access; the frontend calls `POST /api/access` once per session per requirement.
- Never return `price_eur` from option lists. Confidential texts are fine (localhost only). No CORS.

## Meta & state
GET /api/meta → { actor_default, vehicles:{F70:"1 Series",...}, markets:{US:"USA",...}, market_names:{US:"United States",...},
  lines:{"1 Series":{derivatives:[...],segment}}, targets:[Target], focus_targets:[key], successor_launch:{...},
  labels:{evidence, evidence_help, kano, horizon, status, proposal_kinds, verdicts, fit_types, realization},
  priority_bands:{Must:60, Should:45}, scoring:{version, default_weights, factor_labels, confidence, effort_mod, market_fit_mod},
  editable_fields:[...], enums:{horizon:[...], kano_class:[...], effort:["S","M","L"]}, waves:{ "1":{label,simulated_date,description},...},
  zones:{id:{label,pos:[f,r,h],view:[f,r,h],dist}} }
GET /api/state → { current_wave, wave:{label,simulated_date,description}|null, next_wave:int|null, waves_opened:[{wave,ts,actor}],
  spend_usd, budget:{warn,block_non_demo,hard_stop,total:100}, running_job:{id,kind}|null,
  counts:{to_review, open_proposals, open_by_kind:{priority,content,link_finding,new_requirement,extend,status}, decided, approved, requirements, runs} }

## Briefing (home)
GET /api/briefing → {
  wave:{n,label,simulated_date}, run:{id,ts,trigger,initiated_by}|null, previous_run_id|null,
  headline: { new_requirements:int, priority_changes:int /* AI band changes vs previous run across targets */,
              risers:int, fallers:int, merges_open:int, conflicts:int /* requirements whose targets disagree by ≥2 bands or spread ≥20 */ },
  movers:[{req_id,title,target:Target,score_old,score_new,delta,priority_old,priority_new,cause}] (top 8 by |delta| between the last two runs),
  new_requirements:[{req_id,title,category,max_score,best_target:Target,reason}] (proposals kind new_requirement from latest wave, any status, newest first, ≤6),

                req_id, title, subtitle, score:float|null, priority:str|null, target:Target|null, created_at, run_id|null }
  Order: proposals that change an existing decision first (priority, extend), then requirements to review sorted by max score in scope, then content/link proposals. new_requirement proposals are folded INTO the requirement item (field `is_new_in_wave`) — do not list them twice.
GET /api/proposals?status=open|decided|all&kind=&requirement_id= → [Proposal] (inventory §3 shape; plus `target:Target|null`, `finding`, `findings`)

# Successor web — UI kit rules (read before building a screen)

World: "cockpit" — near-black cabin glass, one BMW-like blue for decisions and focus, telltale lights for state,
Fey-level restraint and density. Dark only. No BMW logos. English, current domain terms (`src/lib/labels.ts`).

## Files
- Tokens: `src/styles/tokens.css` (colours, type scale, radii, motion). Base classes: `src/styles/base.css`.
- Primitives: `src/components/ui.tsx` — `PriorityMark` (filled = PM-confirmed, dashed + "AI" = AI suggestion),
  `EvidenceMeter` (signal bars E1–E4), `ScoreBar` (0–100 with ticks at 45/60), `ScoreArc` (headline gauge), `Delta`,
  `StatusLight`, `Seg` (segmented control), `Kbd`, `Skeleton(Block)`, `ErrorNote`, `Empty`, `Stat`.
- Requirement blocks: `src/components/req.tsx` (`DecisionAsk`, `VoiceByMarket`, `Quotes`, `StudyAndWeb`, `Conflict`,
  `MarketTable`, `FitGates`, `AssumptionsBlock`, `ReqTags`).
- Actions: `src/components/actions.tsx` (`ReasonField`, `reasonOk`, `useJob`, `ChallengeDrawer`, `OverrideDrawer`).
- Shell: `PageHead` from `src/components/Shell.tsx`; `Drawer` for side detail; `useToast()` for confirmations.
- Data: `api.get/post/put/patch` + `qs()` from `src/lib/api.ts`, TanStack Query (`useQuery` with stable keys),
  `invalidateAll()` after every write. Types in `src/lib/types.ts` (extend there, don't redefine locally).
- Formatting: `src/lib/format.ts`. Labels: `src/lib/labels.ts` (`car()`, `mkt()`, `targetLabel()`, EVIDENCE, KANO…).

## Layout
- A screen is `<main className="page">` → `PageHead` → content. Bottom padding already clears the floating dock.
- Containers: `.panel` (+ `.panel-head` / `.panel-body`). ONE level only — never a panel inside a panel, never a
  "card grid" of identical icon+title+text tiles. Group with whitespace, rules (`.rule`) and type instead.
- Tables: `.table` (+ `.clickable` rows, `.r` for numbers). Numbers always tabular (`.num`).
- Controls: `.btn` (`.btn-primary` for the one main action per view, `.btn-ghost`, `.btn-danger`, `.btn-sm`),
  `.input`, `.textarea`, `.select`, `Seg`. Chips: `.chip` (+ `up` `down` `warn` `blue` `violet` `outline`).
  Telltales: `.telltale` (+ `blue` `amber` `red` `green` `violet`).
- Headings: `t-head` (page), `t-title` (section/drawer), `panel-head h2` (14px). No eyebrow/kicker labels above
  headings, no section numbers, no gradient text, no coloured side borders, no glow halos, no emoji.
- Big numbers: `.instrument` (wide, light) — only for genuine readouts (scores, counts that matter).

## Behaviour
- Every write needs a reason (`ReasonField`, ≥5 chars) and shows a toast "… Recorded in the audit trail.".
- Loading: skeletons, not spinners. Errors: `ErrorNote` with retry. Empty: `Empty` with what to do next.
- Links between screens: requirements → `/requirements/:id`; cars → `/cars/:vehicle?market=XX`;
  markets → `/markets/:code`; decisions → `/decide/req:REQ-0001`.
- Keyboard first where it helps; respect reduced motion (tokens already zero durations).
- Never show option-list prices. Customer quotes are confidential but fine on this localhost app.

379	def waterfall(b: dict) -> list[dict]:
380	    """Score arithmetic as steps: factor points (without confidence), the confidence cut, modifiers, total."""
381	    facs = (b or {}).get("factors") or {}
382	    if not facs:
383	        return []
384	    conf = float(b.get("confidence") or 1.0)
385	    wsum = sum(f["weight"] for f in facs.values() if f.get("available")) or 1
386	    rows, run = [], 0.0
387	    for key, f in facs.items():
388	        if not f.get("available"):
389	            continue
390	        pts = 100 * f["weight"] * (f["value"] or 0) / wsum
391	        rows.append({"step": f["label"], "factor": key, "kind": "factor", "start": round(run, 2),
392	                     "end": round(run + pts, 2), "delta": round(pts, 2)})
393	        run += pts
394	    cut = run * (1 - conf)
395	    if cut >= 0.05:
396	        rows.append({"step": f"Evidence confidence ×{conf}", "factor": None, "kind": "minus", "start": round(run - cut, 2),
397	                     "end": round(run, 2), "delta": round(-cut, 2)})
398	        run -= cut
399	    for k, val in (b.get("modifiers") or {}).items():
400	        if val:
401	            rows.append({"step": k.replace("_", " ").capitalize(), "factor": None, "kind": "plus" if val > 0 else "minus",
402	                         "start": round(min(run, run + val), 2), "end": round(max(run, run + val), 2),
403	                         "delta": round(val, 2)})
404	            run += val
405	    rows.append({"step": "Score", "factor": None, "kind": "total", "start": 0, "end": float(b.get("score", run)),
406	                 "delta": float(b.get("score", run))})
407	    return rows

The new app is built and running at **http://127.0.0.1:8600**. Streamlit is gone from the new UI: it's a React web app with real-time three.js 3D, on top of a small FastAPI layer over your existing Python pipeline. The 3D car models are still missing, so the Cars screen shows a placeholder car until you log in to Sketchfab or download the three files (as I said above).

**The new workflow** (floating dock at the bottom, ⌘K search everywhere):
- **Briefing:** what the last wave changed, compiled from the data with no AI call. Also shows a car × market overview, the biggest score moves, and a feed of recent events.
- **Decide:** one queue for everything that needs you: AI priority changes, merges, requirements to review and AI edits. Step through it with J/K, choose with A/D/R, give a reason, record with ⌘↵. Overriding a brand-fit failure and "Ask the AI" are on the same screen.
- **Cars:** today's car in a 3D studio with each requirement pinned where customers experience it. Clicking a zone flies the camera there, and for interior zones the body turns see-through. Each zone also lists what today's car already offers there. Below: how the same car ranks across markets, the market profile, competitors and plants.
- **Markets:** who that market's customers are, what they ask of each car, where they disagree with the other markets, and cited competitor and trend signals.
- **Requirement page:** score per market as a gauge, the score arithmetic, its history across runs, and the evidence chain down to the original customer comment. "Trace step by step" replaces the old "How it works" page.
- **Evidence:** the findings library, themes no requirement covers yet, and the quality hand-over list.
- **Process:** wave timeline with "open next wave", runs and weights, the audit trail, the deliverable export, budget and demo snapshots.
- **Present** (top band): story mode that walks the BMW pitch over the live app in 11 steps.

**Design:** the dark "Cockpit" direction you picked. One BMW-like blue for decisions, coloured status lights for state, wide light numerals like an instrument cluster. A priority you confirmed is drawn filled; an AI suggestion is drawn dashed with an "AI" tag. There is no BMW logo; the product is called "Successor".

**Verification:**
- 74 tests pass, including 19 new API tests, and the production build works.
- I ran the full decision flow in a browser against a copy of the database: approved one requirement with a reason, which confirmed 8 market priorities and wrote the audit entries. The demo database is untouched, and no OpenAI calls were made.
- An independent design review found 8 problems. I fixed six fully and two partly, plus three new issues the first fix round caused.
- **Still open:** on a phone-width screen the Requirement page is 24px too wide, which clips the search button in the top band. I couldn't find the cause within the review budget.

content.text:
The three cars are now real 3D models in the app, at http://127.0.0.1:8600/cars/G60?market=US.

- **Files:** I **copied** them rather than moved them, because the project rules treat `challange information document/` as read-only. They're now `data/models/f70.glb` (47 MB), `g60.glb` (15 MB) and `g70.glb` (8.9 MB). That folder is git-ignored, so they won't be committed. You can delete the originals whenever you like.
- **Orientation:** I set which way each model faces and rendered all three to check. The nose points front-left, the wheels sit on the studio floor, and the pins land on the right areas (grille, windscreen, cockpit, roof, doors, trunk).
- **Interior view:** clicking an interior area such as the rear cabin on the 5 Series LWB (China) makes the body see-through, and the rear-seat recommendation sits on the rear seats.
- The 5 Series LWB reuses the 5 Series model, and the screen says so. Each car shows its Sketchfab credit.
- All 74 tests pass, and I updated the open question about the models (Q-025) and the project state notes.

The 1 Series model is AI-generated: its paint has a crumpled, chrome-like texture next to the cleaner 5 and 7 Series. It works, but if it bothers you for the pitch I can look for a better 1 Series model.
